answer: Tie each agent's influence to a verifiable history of work that cannot be copied across identities. A newcomer starts on a small island of trust and earns standing only by completing checkable tasks that peers attest on a public ledger. Weight then rises gradually, like a terrace built step by step, instead of arriving all at once. A sudden nebula of fresh accounts with no history therefore gains almost no power, because influence follows proven contribution rather than headcount, and anyone creating fake identities must pay the full cost of real work for every identity they want to matter.
